messages:
Sanjay Patel: handing off to @Mei. quick recap of the evening regional failover and current posture: we had an automated routing spill from eu-west to eu-central at ~20:12 UTC after the eu-west edge LB started dropping healthchecks. impact: increased p95 latency (~800ms -> ~1.8s) for ~6% of hosted requests for ~22m, a small number of users saw incomplete streams. pages: 3 total (2 automated, 1 manual). mitigation actions taken:

Mei Chen: noted root cause looked like a gradual TLS cert rotation bug in the load balancer agent, it failed to renew for 2 nodes and healthchecks started failing. we flipped routing policy for affected prefix to prefer dedicated pools in eu-central and forced a short re-provision of 2 eu-west nodes.

Alex Rivera: confirmed fallback model variant was applied for long-tail requests to keep latency under SLA for priority customers. I sent a heads-up to top-5 affected customers (support ticket numbers: #23458, #23463).

Sanjay Patel: commands I ran (for reference):
```
# quick view of routing spill
curl -sS https://internal-routing.redwood/api/status?region=eu-west | jq .
# force re-provision for node group
rbctl nodes reprovision --group eu-west-edge --limit 2
```

Elena Gomez: current status: eu-west healthchecks stabilized at 20:34 UTC after reprovision, traffic gradually flowed back by 20:40 UTC. routing policy remains in "prefer-dedicated" for the prefix for 30m to monitor. no active pages. customer-impact: degraded latency window ~22m, partial stream truncation reported in 3 sessions total.

oncall-bot: incident summary created -> https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-2792 (auto-attach: logs, traces, alert graphs).

Mei Chen: runbook tie-ins: follow these runbooks in order -> /runbooks/regional-failover.md, /runbooks/edge-cert-rotation.md. TL;DR: check cert expiry on edge agent, rotate certs with `rbctl cert rotate --group eu-west`, and validate healthchecks with `rbctl health check eu-west`.

Sanjay Patel: assignments for next shift: Mei is primary for the night (primary: Mei Chen), Alex is secondary (secondary: Alex Rivera). Elena will take customer comms follow-up and coordinate with support. I've left checklists in the incident doc for the postmortem: timeline + what we toggled.

Alex Rivera: quick notes for tomorrow: capture node-agent logs for the 2 reprovisioned nodes, compare agent version and cert keystore timestamps. I'll spin up a query tomorrow morning to look for similar cert rotation failures across regions.

Mei Chen: next immediate steps (me): monitor routing metrics for 2h, set an alert for repeated TLS renew failures (threshold: >1 node fail in 5m), and start a short RCA draft. if anything flares, page @Sanjay.

Sanjay Patel: a couple of action-items for oncall handoff sheet: 1) add cert-rotation smoke test to canary pipeline 2) add a backlog ticket to audit agent auto-renew logic 3) include dedicated-pool fallback as a documented mitigation step in the runbook.

Elena Gomez: noted. I'll update the customer email drafts for the affected accounts and assign follow-ups in support.

Alex Rivera: LGTM. :thumbsup:

Mei Chen: handing over active watch to @Alex in 2h if no regressions. good handoff.

Sanjay Patel: thanks all — leaving the thread. (reaction :white_check_mark:)
